svg.title: Other airspace areas
svg.desc: Cards for local airport advisory, military training routes, temporary flight restrictions, parachute jump operations, published VFR routes, terminal radar service areas, national security areas and special VFR, plus a list of the other areas PHAK names such as the ADIZ, flight restricted zones, parks, tethered balloons, ultralights and unmanned balloons.
svg.text: Other airspace areas
"Other airspace areas" is the general term for most of the remaining airspace. PHAK lists these and
describes the ones below.
Local airport advisory (LAA)
Advisory service from a Flight Service Station on
the landing airport, on a discrete ground-to-air
frequency or the tower frequency when the tower is
closed.
Includes local advisories, automated weather with
voice broadcast, and ASOS/AWOS data.
Military training routes (MTRs)
Used by military aircraft for tactical flying,
usually below 10,000 ft MSL at over 250 knots.
Named IR (IFR) or VR (VFR) plus a number. Four
digits: no segment above 1,500 ft AGL (IR1206,
VR1207). Three digits: at least one segment above
IR routes are flown under IFR in any weather.
Temporary flight restrictions (TFR)
Set by an FDC NOTAM starting "FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS":
location, time, area in statute miles, altitudes,
coordination facility, reason.
Reasons include hazards, disaster relief,
sightseeing congestion, protecting the President or
public figures, space operations.
Pilot must check NOTAMs in flight planning;
www.tfr.faa.gov. Incursions have led to security
investigations and certificate suspensions.
Parachute jump aircraft operations
Published in the Chart Supplement U.S.; frequently
used sites are shown on sectionals.
No jump in or into Class A, B, C or D without ATC
authorization from the facility having jurisdiction
(14 CFR part 105).
Published VFR routes
For transitioning around, under or through complex
airspace.
Called VFR flyway, VFR corridor, Class B VFR
transition route or terminal area VFR route.
Generally found on VFR terminal area planning
charts.
Terminal radar service areas (TRSAs)
Participating pilots get added radar service that
separates all IFR from participating VFR aircraft.
Primary airport becomes Class D; the rest overlies
mostly Class E starting at 700 or 1,200 ft.
Charted with a solid black line and altitudes;
Class D part has a blue segmented line.
Voluntary, but VFR pilots are encouraged to call
radar approach control.
National security areas (NSAs)
Defined airspace where ground facilities need more
security and safety.
Flight may be temporarily prohibited under 14 CFR
part 99, by NOTAM.
Pilots are asked to voluntarily avoid flying
through depicted areas.
Special VFR
14 CFR 91.157 is the exception to the rule that VFR
flight beneath a ceiling under 1,000 ft is not
allowed within controlled airspace designated to
the surface for an airport.
Also in the list, and nearby rules
ADIZ (land and water based): a Defense VFR (DVFR) flight plan is needed to fly VFR in it. Intercept
procedures: use 121.5 MHz if not already on ATC.
Flight Restricted Zones near the Capitol and White House. Special awareness training (14 CFR 91.161) to fly
VFR within 60 NM of the Washington, DC VOR/DME.
Wildlife, wilderness areas and national parks: request to stay above 2,000 ft AGL. NOAA marine areas off the
coast: above 2,000 ft AGL.
Tethered balloons for observation and weather recording, on cables up to 60,000 (the text gives no unit).
Ultralights (part 103) need prior ATC authorization in Class A to D and the surface area of airport Class E.
Unmanned free balloons below 2,000 ft above the surface need ATC authorization in B, C, D or airport Class E
(part 101).
